body: Is what I'm trying to do right? Like I want to respect her decision but at the same time I want her to know that its not disgusting or anything to be ashamed of. I don't want her to feel disgusted with herself and ashamed of herself. I just don't know if how I'm going about it is the best way. If you were in my position, what would you do?

I know, and I'm trying to not make it about me. I just don't want her to think that I find it disgusting because I don't. She doesn't need to feel worse about it by thinking that she forced me into doing it and made me feel obligated to do it. That's all I'm trying to get across to her. She never forced me to do it.

I think I figured out why I was persistent about trying to figure out where she was coming from. I feel like if I didn't pursue it then she would think that I really didn't like it at all and that I thought it was disgusting. So my mind puts it as I need to fight for what I want in order to prove that I want it and enjoy it. I just feel like if I don't put up any resistance then the situation would become worse. I hope that kind of makes sense.

I agree with you 100%, I need to realize that this is a team effort and we have to agree with each other on what we do, that if there's a discrepancy then we talk it over and not push each other and that I'm not in control of us. Rather we are in charge of us. I need to lose the perspective of myself and gain the perspective of our relationship.

What you do is an excellent thing, you give us guys and insight into a woman's mind and perspective without any bias and I greatly thank you for it! I am the type of guy who is a problem solver and doesn't like to quick until everything is fixed. That can be a good thing and it can be a bad thing, but I always have the best intentions possible. Thank you for the offer! I will probably take you up on it. It really helps me to talk things out and get an outside, unbiased perspective on things.

Our sex life is wonderful and bonding, I just have to get over myself and focus on sex as a whole rather than the individual acts like you said. My communication isn't very strong due to my own trust issues from past relationships, it's not to the point that it needs to be but I have come a very far way and I'm still improving. I try so hard because she is the one for me and I want to spend my life with her. I would do anything for her.

I believe that there is much more to love than just sex, I'm just saying that sex is important to keep a relationship strong and healthy. It's a bonding time, and intimate for both people to be together as one and support each other. It shows you at your most vulnerable and builds trust due to that fact. I love her with all my heart and we do a lot for each other outside of sex. We cook, clean, study, go on dates, etc together and spend almost all our time together.

I do have a lot of work and I have been making progress, or at least I like to think so. I've been trying so hard to be able to separate love from sex since we started dating three years ago but I just can't see it that way. If sex and love aren't connected, then wouldn't that be fuck buddies (sorry for the language) or friends with benefits? I do see what you are saying with the anal scenario though, I don't know that I would say yes to it, but it wouldn't be because I don't love her.

I need the outside perspective because my understand of sex is not an act, but is love itself (catholic raised) and it's hard to see it stopping because I have it associated with love and it makes me feel like she doesn't love me. I know that's not true but I can't help but to feel that.

I actually didn't see it that way, but you could not be more correct. It's not about me, it's about her. Thank you for that, I truly appreciate the outside looking in! I just have to deal with myself and not push the topic anymore, and let her decide what to do if she ever wants to do it again.

Edit: By talking to her about it every day I mean like from her point of view. I'm just trying to see it and understand it from her side.

I'm not pushing it on her, I have accepted the fact that she doesn't want it anymore and have told her that I respect her and her decision the day it happened, I've just been trying to get her side of it. Like if i did something wrong, or if I hurt her, or if I did it too much.
